# T4 evidence: web asset budgets

## Deliverables

- `scripts/quality/assets.mjs`: reporter and checker. Uses only Node built-ins (`fs`, `path`, `zlib`, `crypto`, `child_process`).
- `quality/web-budgets.json`: profile definitions, baseline values, numeric budgets, policy, and capture metadata.
- `tests/quality/assets.test.mjs`: `node:test` suite that runs on synthetic fixtures in temporary directories.
- Archives (ignored, under `build/`): `build/eng-baseline/1b8d4332/web-default/` and `web-modern/`. Each holds `dist/`, `config.json`, `sha256sums.txt`, `report.json` (with metrics and dependency composition), `build.log`, and `build-sourcemaps.log`.
- Raw check logs: `build/eng-artifacts/T4/` (`red.log`, `green.log`, `check-*.log`).

## How profiles are selected

The profile flags come from `web/vite.config.js` and `docs/BUILD.md`. No CMake or Docker flags are involved: the Dockerfile and install scripts run plain `npm run build`.

| Profile | Command (cwd `web/`) | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | `npm run build` | Uses `@vitejs/plugin-legacy` (`defaults, not IE 11`, `modernPolyfills: true`), so the output has modern and legacy (SystemJS) chunks. All 18 locales are included. |
| `modern` | `LIGHTNVR_WEB_LEGACY=false npm run build` | Modern-only output: the legacy plugin is not loaded. All 18 locales are included. |

`LIGHTNVR_WEB_LOCALES=en` (from the firmware example in `docs/BUILD.md`) controls a separate setting. It is not part of either profile. Its effect can be estimated from `installed.locales.perLocale.*`: dropping every locale except `en` saves 4,651,121 − 243,817 − manifest bytes.

Before each build, `--capture` removes any environment variable that changes the output (`LIGHTNVR_WEB_*`, `SENTRY_*`, `VITE_SENTRY_*`, `BUILD_SOURCEMAPS`). It then applies only the profile's own env. `--check` confirms that the profile actually took effect:
- legacy chunks and `nomodule` entries must be present for `default` and absent for `modern`
- the locale set must match `web/public/locales/manifest.json`
- all 11 entry pages must exist

## Revisions

- Plan baseline: `1b8d4332`. `git diff --stat 1b8d4332 8927bc8a -- web/` is empty, and so is `git diff --stat 1b8d4332 HEAD -- web/` at commit time. #692 (SPDX headers) changed only C sources.
- The `default` archive was built at `7db92e0d` and the `modern` archive at `ff6a7d60` (T1 committed between the two captures). Both had a web/ tree identical to `1b8d4332`. `--capture` refuses to run when web/ differs from `1b8d4332` or has uncommitted or untracked changes.
- The ignored, generated `web/js/version.js` contains `GIT_COMMIT = '7db92e0d'`. Its exact contents are recorded in each `config.json`. It was not regenerated between captures.
- Toolchain: node v24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, vite 8.3.5, linux-x64. Install was `npm ci --prefix web` (lockfile sha256 `4563ca16…4879`).
- Reproducibility: two separate `npm run build` runs of the same tree produced identical sha256 values for all 221 files.

## Commands run (repo root)

```
npm ci --prefix web
node --test tests/quality/assets.test.mjs          # RED: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (build/eng-artifacts/T4/red.log)
node scripts/quality/assets.mjs --capture --profile default
node scripts/quality/assets.mjs --capture --profile modern
node scripts/quality/assets.mjs --propose --profile <p> --from build/eng-baseline/1b8d4332/web-<p>/report.json
node --test tests/quality/assets.test.mjs          # GREEN: 9/9 pass (green.log)
(cd web && LIGHTNVR_WEB_LEGACY=false npm run build) && node scripts/quality/assets.mjs --check --profile modern   # exit 0, 43 budgets
(cd web && npm run build) && node scripts/quality/assets.mjs --check --profile default                           # exit 0, 66 budgets
```

Negative checks on the real tree:
- Running `--check --profile default` against a modern dist exits 1 with a profile mismatch and unknown legacy metrics.
- Running `touch web/js/version.js` and then `--check` exits 1 with "stale build: web/js/version.js … newer than dist".
- Temporarily removing `assets/sentry-*.js` makes `--check` exit 1 with "missing artifact … referenced by …".

## Byte accounting rules

The checker uses four byte measures and never mixes them:

- **installed**: every file in dist counted once, including the shipped `.gz` copies, locales (`.json`, `.json.gz`, `.png`), CSS copies, and icons.
- **served**: the precompressed `.gz` sibling if one exists, otherwise the raw file. This is what `src/web/libuv_connection.c` sends to a gzip-capable browser.
- **gzip**: zlib level 9, computed by the checker.
- **brotli**: quality 11. Informational only, because the server does not serve brotli.

How pages and chunks are measured:
- **Page cost:** the static import closure of the HTML's module or legacy entry scripts, plus `modulepreload` links, stylesheets, and icons. The checker resolves `import … from`, `export … from`, `System.register([...])`, `import()`, `t.import()`, and `__vite__mapDeps` preload lists. Every aggregate is computed over a set of files, so a chunk shared by several pages is counted once per total. The `chunks.shared` rows list each shared chunk once, with the pages that use it.
- **Vite manifest:** not used, because the unchanged `vite.config.js` does not set `build.manifest`, and changing config is out of scope. The HTML and chunk parsing is checked by tests. Any reference that cannot be resolved is reported as a missing artifact.
- **Dependency composition:** taken from a separate `BUILD_SOURCEMAPS=true` pass run before the production pass. Mapped generated bytes are attributed to the source package. All 56/56 (default) and 27/27 (modern) chunk names matched the production pass. The output of that pass is discarded.

Findings:
- No page lazy-loads JS. `hls.js` is bundled statically into the shared `LiveView` chunk, which is the largest cost on the Live and HLS pages.
- The 117,751 B of raw `css/*.css` copies (the `copy-css-files` plugin) are installed but are not referenced by any emitted page.

## Budgets and rationale

Budgets follow the formulas below. `--propose` prints them to stdout from an archived `report.json`, and `quality/web-budgets.json` was assembled from that output.

- totals (`installed.*`, `transfer.*`, `chunks.*`): `ceil(max(baseline × 1.03, baseline + 4096))`
- per page (`entries.*`): `ceil(max(baseline × 1.05, baseline + 2048))`

Because the build is reproducible byte for byte, the headroom is not there to absorb noise. It only allows small incidental growth from typed refactors. Anything larger fails:
- about 20 KiB gzip added to the Live page (5% of 397,094)
- about 18 KiB added to the served modern JS total (3% of 604,760)

Budgeted metrics:
- `default`: 66. These cover installed, original, `.gz` and locale bytes; unique modern/legacy/CSS/HTML transfer; shared-chunk bytes; and for each page, served modern firstLoad, initialJs and initialCss, plus legacy firstLoad and initialJs.
- `modern`: 43. These are the same metrics without the legacy ones.

## Guarantees

- `--check` only reads. It has no code path that writes. A test confirms that the budgets file keeps the same content and mtime after a failing check, and that no sidecar files appear.
- `--capture` never writes the budgets file. It refuses to overwrite an existing archive unless `--force` is given.
- A check fails if:
  - the profile has no budgets, or a budget is not a positive integer
  - a budget names a metric the dist does not produce
  - `dist/` or an entry page is missing
  - a referenced chunk or CSS file is missing
  - `locales/manifest.json` is missing
  - the build is stale (any `web/{js,css,img,fonts,public}/**`, `web/*.html`, Vite/PostCSS/Tailwind config, `package*.json`, or `node_modules/.package-lock.json` is newer than the oldest emitted HTML page)
  - the profile flags are not reflected in the output
  - any metric exceeds its budget

## RED → GREEN

- RED (`build/eng-artifacts/T4/red.log`): `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND … scripts/quality/assets.mjs`. The suite failed before the implementation existed.
- GREEN (`build/eng-artifacts/T4/green.log`): 9/9 pass. The tests cover:
  - installed vs served vs gzip/brotli accounting, with no double counting of shared chunks
  - the per-page closure for both modern and legacy graphs
  - a missing dist, entry, or chunk causing a failure
  - a stale dist causing a failure
  - a profile mismatch causing a failure
  - an oversized fixture (+200 KB) causing a failure
  - an unknown metric or an empty budget set causing a failure
  - the CLI exit codes, and the budgets file staying untouched
  - parser edge cases

## Notes for downstream (T5, T8, T15, T24, T36)

- Run `--check` right after building the matching profile. `web/dist` holds only one profile at a time, so a dist built for the other profile fails as a mismatch.
- Run `npm ci` before building, not after. `node_modules/.package-lock.json` is treated as a build input, so installing after the build marks the dist as stale.
- `npm ci` warns that the install scripts for esbuild, core-js and unrs-resolver were not run (they are not covered by `allowScripts`). The builds succeed regardless.
- A full check takes about 7 s, mostly brotli quality 11 on the locale files.
- Raising a budget means editing `quality/web-budgets.json` by hand, with the measured cost and the product reason.
